REGRA EDITORIAL, e não é decorativa: nada aqui pode ser sobre metadados.
Contagens de linhas, tabelas mais usadas e resumos de esquema estão
proibidos. Foi exactamente esse tipo de resposta — 'resumo de alto nível:
contagem de linhas e tabelas mais usadas' — que arruinou a primeira
impressão da demo antiga. Cada título aqui responde a uma pergunta que um
COO faria em voz alta, e cada número tem SQL por trás que o produz.
O `executed_sql` não é decoração: é verificado contra a base sintética
antes de persistir (--verify-sql). Conteúdo que afirme um número que o
seu próprio SQL não devolve é pior do que não ter conteúdo nenhum — numa
demo comercial, um número errado que o prospect consegue conferir custa

insight.title: Enterprise accounts paying for seats they stopped using
insight.summary: Enterprise accounts are billing more seats than they log into. Seat utilisation is the earliest churn signal there is — it moves months before the cancellation email, and it is visible today across CRM, billing and product usage at once.

qas.question: Which customers are most likely to churn, and what revenue is at stake?
qas.answer_markdown:
**Oscorp Industries, Cogswell Inc and Wonka Group** carry the most revenue at risk — all flagged risk or churn by health score, and all still paying.

What makes this actionable rather than interesting: it joins the health signal to the money. A low score on a small account is noise; the same score on the largest subscription in the book is a board-level problem.

They are paying today. That is the window.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT a.name,
       a.plan,
       h.risk_level,
       h.score,
       s.monthly_amount,
       h.last_login_at
FROM product_usage.account_health h
JOIN crm.accounts a         ON a.id = h.account_id
JOIN finance.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.id AND s.cancelled_at IS NULL
WHERE h.risk_level IN ('risk', 'churn')
ORDER BY s.monthly_amount DESC
LIMIT 10

qas.question: Which marketing channel actually produces revenue, not just leads?
qas.answer_markdown:
Spend per channel against **closed-won** revenue traced back through the lead that opened the deal.

The distinction matters. Channels that produce many leads and few deals look excellent on a marketing dashboard and lose money in the ledger — the cost per lead is flattering, the cost per euro of revenue is not.

This follows the chain end to end: campaign spend → lead → opportunity → closed-won amount.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT c.channel,
       SUM(DISTINCT c.spend)                                    AS spend,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.id)                                     AS leads,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won') AS deals_won,
       COALESCE(SUM(o.amount) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won'), 0) AS revenue_won
FROM marketing.campaigns c
LEFT JOIN marketing.leads l   ON l.campaign_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN crm.opportunities o ON o.id = l.converted_to_opportunity_id
GROUP BY c.channel
ORDER BY revenue_won DESC

qas.question: How much revenue is sitting in overdue invoices, and who owes it?
qas.answer_markdown:
Invoices past due, by account, oldest first.

Cash that has been earned and not collected is the cheapest cash in the business — no discount, no new deal, no campaign. It only needs someone to know it exists.

The join to the account name is the whole point: an invoice ID is not something anyone can act on, a customer name with a phone number is.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT a.name,
       i.issued_at,
       i.amount,
       CURRENT_DATE - i.issued_at AS days_outstanding
FROM finance.invoices i
JOIN finance.subscriptions s ON s.id = i.subscription_id
JOIN crm.accounts a          ON a.id = s.account_id
WHERE i.status = 'overdue'
ORDER BY i.issued_at ASC
LIMIT 15

qas.question: What is the win rate, and how long does a deal take to close?
qas.answer_markdown:
Win rate and average cycle length per plan tier.

The two numbers belong together. A high win rate with a long cycle and a lower win rate with a short one are very different businesses, and reporting either alone hides which one you are.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT a.plan,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won')  AS won,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_lost') AS lost,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won')
             / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage IN ('closed_won','closed_lost')), 0), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(o.amount) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won'), 2) AS avg_won_amount
FROM crm.opportunities o
JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.id = o.account_id
GROUP BY a.plan
ORDER BY win_rate_pct DESC NULLS LAST

qas.question: Which product features do our healthiest customers use that the at-risk ones don't?
qas.answer_markdown:
Feature adoption split by health band.

The gap between the two columns is the onboarding backlog. A feature that healthy accounts use heavily and at-risk accounts never touched is not a product problem — it is a feature nobody showed them.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT f.feature_name,
       ROUND(AVG(f.times_used_30d) FILTER (WHERE h.risk_level = 'healthy'), 1)          AS healthy_avg_uses,
       ROUND(AVG(f.times_used_30d) FILTER (WHERE h.risk_level IN ('risk','churn')), 1)  AS at_risk_avg_uses,
       COUNT(DISTINCT f.account_id)                                                     AS accounts_using
FROM product_usage.feature_adoption f
JOIN product_usage.account_health h ON h.account_id = f.account_id
GROUP BY f.feature_name
ORDER BY healthy_avg_uses DESC NULLS LAST

qas.question: How has new business trended over the last year?
qas.answer_markdown:
Closed-won revenue by month.

The shape matters more than the total. A book that grows in steps — a flat stretch, then a jump — is a business that closes a few large deals, and it needs a different forecast than one that grows smoothly.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.close_date)::date AS month,
       COUNT(*)                                    AS deals_won,
       SUM(o.amount)                               AS revenue_won
FROM crm.opportunities o
WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

qas.question: Where does our website traffic come from, and does it convert?
qas.answer_markdown:
Sessions by acquisition source against the accounts that ended up signing.

Traffic without the conversion column is a vanity number. The two together tell you which source to buy more of.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT COALESCE(s.utm_source, 'direct')                     AS source,
       COUNT(*)                                            AS sessions,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.account_id)                        AS known_accounts,
       ROUND(AVG(s.pages_viewed), 1)                       AS avg_pages
FROM web_analytics.sessions s
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY sessions DESC

qas.answer_markdown:
**Oscorp Industries, Cogswell Inc e Wonka Group** são as três com maior receita em risco — todas marcadas como risco ou saída pelo indicador de saúde, e todas ainda a pagar.

O que torna isto accionável em vez de interessante: liga o sinal de saúde ao dinheiro. Um indicador baixo numa conta pequena é ruído; o mesmo indicador na maior subscrição da carteira é assunto de administração.

Estão a pagar hoje. É essa a janela.

qas.question: Que canal de marketing produz receita a sério, e não só leads?
qas.answer_markdown:
Investimento por canal contra a receita **ganha**, seguida até ao lead que abriu o negócio.

A distinção importa. Canais que produzem muitos leads e poucos negócios ficam excelentes num relatório de marketing e perdem dinheiro no livro de contas — o custo por lead é lisonjeiro, o custo por euro de receita não é.

Isto segue a cadeia até ao fim: investimento na campanha → lead → oportunidade → valor ganho.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT c.channel,
       SUM(DISTINCT c.spend)                                    AS spend,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.id)                                     AS leads,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won') AS deals_won,
       COALESCE(SUM(o.amount) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won'), 0) AS revenue_won
FROM marketing.campaigns c
LEFT JOIN marketing.leads l   ON l.campaign_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN crm.opportunities o ON o.id = l.converted_to_opportunity_id
GROUP BY c.channel
ORDER BY revenue_won DESC

qas.question: Quanta receita está parada em faturas vencidas, e quem as deve?
qas.answer_markdown:
Faturas fora de prazo, por cliente, das mais antigas para as mais recentes.

Dinheiro que já foi ganho e não foi cobrado é o dinheiro mais barato do negócio — sem desconto, sem negócio novo, sem campanha. Só precisa que alguém saiba que existe.

A junção ao nome do cliente é o ponto todo: um número de fatura não é accionável, um nome com um telefone é.

SELECT a.name,
       i.issued_at,
       i.amount,
       CURRENT_DATE - i.issued_at AS days_outstanding
FROM finance.invoices i
JOIN finance.subscriptions s ON s.id = i.subscription_id
JOIN crm.accounts a          ON a.id = s.account_id
WHERE i.status = 'overdue'
ORDER BY i.issued_at ASC
LIMIT 15

qas.question: Qual é a taxa de ganho, e quanto tempo demora a fechar?
qas.answer_markdown:
Taxa de ganho e valor médio por escalão de plano.

Os dois números pertencem um ao outro. Uma taxa alta com ciclo longo e uma taxa mais baixa com ciclo curto são negócios muito diferentes, e mostrar só um esconde qual deles é o teu.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT a.plan,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won')  AS won,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_lost') AS lost,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won')
             / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage IN ('closed_won','closed_lost')), 0), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(o.amount) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won'), 2) AS avg_won_amount
FROM crm.opportunities o
JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.id = o.account_id
GROUP BY a.plan
ORDER BY win_rate_pct DESC NULLS LAST

qas.question: Que funcionalidades os clientes saudáveis usam e os em risco nunca tocaram?
qas.answer_markdown:
Adoção de funcionalidades separada por banda de saúde.

A diferença entre as duas colunas é a lista de espera do onboarding. Uma funcionalidade que as contas saudáveis usam muito e as contas em risco nunca abriram não é um problema de produto — é uma funcionalidade que ninguém lhes mostrou.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT f.feature_name,
       ROUND(AVG(f.times_used_30d) FILTER (WHERE h.risk_level = 'healthy'), 1)          AS healthy_avg_uses,
       ROUND(AVG(f.times_used_30d) FILTER (WHERE h.risk_level IN ('risk','churn')), 1)  AS at_risk_avg_uses,
       COUNT(DISTINCT f.account_id)                                                     AS accounts_using
FROM product_usage.feature_adoption f

qas.question: Which product family is losing margin, and why?
qas.answer_markdown:
**It's the discount, not the cost.** The family with the worst margin is also the one carrying the largest average discount — several times the rest of the catalogue, and applied across the board rather than case by case.

That matters because it changes who fixes it. If it were cost, it'd be a conversation with the supplier; being discount, it's a pricing policy somebody set and nobody revisited.

The number comes from joining two tables nobody joins: the price actually charged is in the order lines, the cost is in the catalogue.

       ROUND(100.0 * AVG(l.discount), 1) AS avg_discount_pct,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(l.quantity * (l.unit_price * (1 - l.discount) - p.unit_cost))
             / NULLIF(SUM(l.quantity * l.unit_price * (1 - l.discount)), 0), 1) AS margin_pct
FROM sales.order_lines l
JOIN catalog.products p ON p.id = l.product_id
GROUP BY p.family
ORDER BY margin_pct

qas.question: Which sales channel gives the most margin — resale, horeca, retail or online?

**The channel that bills most isn't the one that keeps most.** The order changes depending on whether you look at revenue or margin, and that difference is what decides where the sales effort goes.

Revenue without margin beside it is a vanity metric: it grows, it feels good, and it doesn't tell you whether the business got better.

       ROUND(SUM(l.quantity * l.unit_price * (1 - l.discount))) AS revenue,

FROM sales.orders o
JOIN sales.customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN sales.order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.id
JOIN catalog.products p ON p.id = l.product_id
GROUP BY c.channel
ORDER BY margin_pct DESC

insight.title: Um quarto das horas pagas não chega a ser faturável

A capacidade não se perde de uma vez — perde-se meia hora de cada vez, em trabalho interno, pré-venda e formação, que ninguém regista como problema porque cada peça é razoável. Só a soma é que não é.

qas.question: Que máquina está a fazer mais refugo?
qas.answer_markdown:
**Uma só, e com folga.** A taxa dela está numa ordem de grandeza diferente da média das restantes, e é também a mais antiga do parque.

Isto muda a conversa: com uma taxa média de fábrica, a resposta é "temos de melhorar a qualidade", que não tem dono. Com a máquina identificada, é uma decisão de manutenção ou de substituição, com um número ao lado.

Cruza o refugo registado pela qualidade com as ordens de produção — dois sistemas, uma resposta.

       SUM(s.units) AS scrap_units,
       SUM(o.planned_units) AS planned_units,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(s.units) / NULLIF(SUM(o.planned_units), 0), 2) AS scrap_pct
FROM quality.scrap s
JOIN production.orders o ON o.id = s.order_id
JOIN plant.machines m ON m.id = o.machine_id
GROUP BY m.code, m.line, m.installed_year
ORDER BY scrap_pct DESC

qas.question: ¿Qué canal de marketing produce ingresos de verdad, y no solo leads?
qas.answer_markdown:
Gasto por canal frente a los ingresos **cerrados**, rastreados hasta el lead que abrió la operación.

La distinción importa. Los canales que producen muchos leads y pocas operaciones lucen excelentes en un panel de marketing y pierden dinero en la contabilidad — el coste por lead es halagador, el coste por euro de ingreso no lo es.

Esto sigue la cadena de punta a punta: gasto de campaña → lead → oportunidad → importe cerrado.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT c.channel,
       SUM(DISTINCT c.spend)                                    AS spend,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.id)                                     AS leads,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won') AS deals_won,
       COALESCE(SUM(o.amount) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won'), 0) AS revenue_won
FROM marketing.campaigns c
LEFT JOIN marketing.leads l   ON l.campaign_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN crm.opportunities o ON o.id = l.converted_to_opportunity_id
GROUP BY c.channel
ORDER BY revenue_won DESC

Unirlo al nombre de la cuenta es justamente el asunto: con un número de factura nadie puede hacer nada; con un nombre de cliente y un teléfono, sí.

qas.question: ¿Cuál es la tasa de cierre, y cuánto tarda en cerrarse una operación?
qas.answer_markdown:
Tasa de cierre y duración media del ciclo por nivel de plan.

Los dos números van juntos. Una tasa alta con un ciclo largo y una tasa más baja con un ciclo corto son negocios muy distintos, y dar cualquiera de los dos por separado esconde cuál de ellos eres.

       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won')  AS won,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_lost') AS lost,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won')
             / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage IN ('closed_won','closed_lost')), 0), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(o.amount) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won'), 2) AS avg_won_amount
FROM crm.opportunities o
JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.id = o.account_id
GROUP BY a.plan
ORDER BY win_rate_pct DESC NULLS LAST

qas.answer_markdown:
**Es el descuento, no el coste.** La familia con peor margen es también la que carga el mayor descuento medio — varias veces el del resto del catálogo, y aplicado de forma general en vez de caso por caso.

Eso importa porque cambia quién lo arregla. Si fuera coste, sería una conversación con el proveedor; siendo descuento, es una política de precios que alguien fijó y nadie revisó.

El número sale de unir dos tablas que nadie une: el precio realmente cobrado está en las líneas de pedido, el coste está en el catálogo.

qas.question: ¿Cuánto dinero hay parado en stock que no se mueve?
qas.answer_markdown:
**Está concentrado en un puñado de referencias.** El dinero inmovilizado está en unos pocos artículos sin movimiento desde hace más de seis meses — y el más antiguo pasa de diez.

El stock parado es el coste más fácil de ignorar porque no aparece en ningún sitio como coste: está pagado, está en el balance, y ahí se queda. Solo la fecha del último movimiento lo delata.

Con una lista así la decisión es operativa: promoción, devolución al proveedor, o darlo de baja. Sin ella, la decisión sencillamente nunca se toma.

qas.answer_markdown:
**Un proveedor destaca, y no por poco.** Su retraso medio está en otro orden de magnitud que el de los demás — el resto entrega prácticamente en la fecha prometida.

Eso es lo que lo hace accionable: no es el mercado, no es la temporada, es un proveedor. El plazo que acordó no es el plazo que cumple — y eso se renegocia con el histórico delante.

La comparación es prometido contra recibido, entrega a entrega.

**Una, por goleada.** Su tasa está a un orden de magnitud de la media del resto, y además es la máquina más vieja de la nave.

Eso cambia la conversación: con una media de planta, la respuesta es «hay que mejorar la calidad», que no tiene dueño. Con la máquina nombrada, es una decisión de mantenimiento o de reposición, con un número al lado.

Une la merma registrada por calidad con las órdenes de producción — dos sistemas, una respuesta.

qas.question: ¿Qué línea de producción rinde mejor?
qas.answer_markdown:
**Por rendimiento, no por volumen.** La línea que hace más unidades no es necesariamente la que menos desperdicia — y el desperdicio se paga dos veces, en material y en tiempo de máquina.

Con tres líneas, la distancia entre ellas es la única comparación interna honesta que existe.

qas.question: ¿Merece la pena seguir con la máquina más vieja?
qas.answer_markdown:
**Antigüedad, cadencia nominal, rendimiento real y horas de parada, en la misma fila.** Es la información que necesita una decisión de inversión, y suele vivir en cuatro sitios distintos.

Una máquina vieja que va bien no es ningún problema. El problema es cuando la antigüedad aparece al lado de la merma y de las paradas — y entonces la cuenta se hace sola.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT m.code, m.installed_year, m.nominal_rate,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(o.good_units) / NULLIF(SUM(o.planned_units), 0), 1) AS yield_pct,
       ROUND(SUM(st.minutes) / 60.0, 1) AS unplanned_hours
FROM plant.machines m
JOIN production.orders o ON o.machine_id = m.id
LEFT JOIN maintenance.stoppages st ON st.machine_id = m.id AND NOT st.planned
GROUP BY m.code, m.installed_year, m.nominal_rate
ORDER BY m.installed_year
